timeline.note: Lancaster County Clerk responded, providing 23 meeting minutes (2018–2026) via AgendaCenter links and a ZIP archive of 12 procurement records (contracts, amendments, and a resolution covering Vigilant Solutions mobile LPR service 2021–2026 and Motorola fixed-camera system 2025–2026, plus an NDOT right-of-way agreement). Respondent: Angela Zocholl, Records Administrator.
Lancaster County Clerk provided payment vouchers for the ALPR/LPR program as an additional tranche of records and declared the request complete.

The Lancaster County Sheriff's Office requested clarification or narrowing, stating that the original request was not sufficiently specific to identify responsive records. The response did not state that responsive records do not exist and did not invoke an exemption for specific administrative records. A narrowed follow-up was submitted on September 14, 2026.

Lancaster County Sheriff's Office denied the narrowed request, again citing insufficient specificity under Neb. Rev. Stat. § 84-712.01(4)(c). The letter, signed by Sheriff Terry T. Wagner and PIO Kelsey Cruz, stated the Office was "unable to provide the records as requested" because "the description provided is nonspecific in nature and does not allow our Office to locate or determine the existence of records responsive." Administrative and judicial review rights noted under Neb. Rev. Stat. § 84-712.03.

The City of Lincoln asked the requester to clarify the use of MuckRock and stated that it likely would withhold certain records under Neb. Rev. Stat. § 84-712.05(5). The City linked LPD's public ALPR transparency page. The response did not identify specific responsive records or state that responsive administrative records do not exist.

The request was narrowed to specified non-investigative administrative records, including prior policy versions, statutory reporting forms, procurement/payment records, and data-sharing/access agreements.
